title: Load a clipboard: one hand holds the clip's lever pressed down while the other slides a loose card under it to the stop
instruction: Clip the yellow card onto the clipboard: under the clip as far as it goes, straight on the board.
context: Loading a clipboard is everyday work in clinics, classrooms, warehouses and site inspections, and it needs two hands doing different things at once. One presses the clip's thumb lever down against its spring (about 12 N) and keeps it pressed, which lifts the jaw and pins the light board to the desk. Meanwhile the other moves a loose sheet too thin to pick up: it slides it flat under the lifted jaw by fingertip friction until its top edge meets the clip's stop, square to the board. Only then is the lever let go, and from then on nothing but the jaw's spring, pressing the sheet against the board, holds it: picked up and tilted, the board must keep the sheet. Let the lever go too soon and the sheet meets a closed jaw and stops at its lip; stop short of the stop or crooked and the sheet is held but not loaded properly.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. Bench: the station's wooden bench. Clipboard (one free object): a Saunders 05612 letter-size clipboard, 1/8 in (3.2) brown hardboard 229 (x) by 318 (y), 249.5 g with its clip, lying flat, its centre at x 200, y 90, its clip end to the left (+y, toward the left arm's base). Clip: a 4 in nickel-plated steel spring clip riveted to the board on its centre line: a base plate 90 wide, 0.8 thick, whose front edge (the stop) is 26 mm from the board's top edge (y 222.8); a hinge pin 14 mm from the top edge (y 234.8), 7 above the board's face; a 92 wide, 0.8 thick steel lever whose jaw reaches 30 down the board to a square turned-down lip (front face at y 204.8, 4 high) that a torsion spring presses onto the board with about 8 N, and whose thumb tab rises 32 deg behind the pin, 24 long, ending in a 4 mm roll 6 past the board's top edge, 19.7 above its face. Pressing the roll down about 12 N lifts the jaw (estimates; see README). Card (free): Neenah Exact Index 110 lb (199 g/m2) canary card stock, 8.5 x 11 in (216 x 279, 0.24, 12 g), lying loose on the board, square to it and centred on x 200, its top edge at y 177.8 (45 short of the stop, 27 short of the lip), its bottom end 33 past the board's bottom edge (y -68.8). Arms start in the ready pose. Seeded runs shift each object up to 10 mm along x and y.
scoring: Judged once both grippers are at least 3 cm from the clipboard and the card and nothing has moved more than 0.5 mm per 0.05 s for 1 s, with the board flat on the bench (within 3 deg). Held by the clamp: the card's top edge is at least 5 mm past the jaw's lip across the lip's 92 mm, the lip rests on the card (0.05 to 1.5 mm off the board), and when the board is then lifted by the middle of its clip end until it stands at 60 deg on its bottom edge (2.5 s) and held there 2 s, the card slips no more than 3 mm (a pencil tick at its top edge shows it). 1.0: held, the card's top edge within 2 mm of the stop at 40 mm either side of the clip's centre line, and its edges within 2 deg of the board's with no corner past a long edge of the board. 0.75: held and only one of those two. 0.5: held only. 0: anything else, including the jaw resting on the board, under 5 mm of card under the jaw, a slip over 3 mm, a hand still on the clip or card, or the clipboard off the bench.
reset_notes: Press the clip's tab, take the card out and lay it back on the board square and centred, its top edge 45 mm short of the stop; lay the clipboard back at its marks. Nothing is consumed or bent.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz, 20 Hz control. The card is one rigid 0.24 mm plate; it always lies supported on the board or under the jaw, where real card stays flat too. The clip is a rigid lever on a sprung hinge; its profile, the spring (8 N on the lip, ~12 N at the tab) and every friction are estimates to be measured. The lip-on-board contact is the hinge's stop. The 60 deg check is an upward force the scorer applies at the board's clip end. The demo reads the board's and card's poses.
